heading: Pilot projects to encourage the use of public-private partnerships committed to addressing food insecurity

tree.heading: In general
tree.text: The Secretary may, on application of eligible entities, approve not more than 10 pilot projects to support public-private partnerships that address food insecurity and poverty.

children.text: an institution of higher education; or
a private entity, as determined by the Secretary; and
the term “public agency” means a department, agency, other unit, or instrumentality of Federal, State, or local government.

tree.heading: Project requirements
tree.text: Projects approved under this section shall—

children.text: be limited to 2 years in length; and
include a collaboration between one or more public agencies and one or more eligible entities that—
improves the effectiveness and impact of the supplemental nutrition assistance program;
develops food security solutions that are specific to the needs of a community or region; and
strengthens the capacity of communities to address food insecurity and poverty.

tree.heading: Evaluation
tree.text: The Secretary shall provide for an independent evaluation of pilot projects approved under this section that includes—

children.text: a summary of the activities conducted under the pilot projects;
an assessment of the effectiveness of the pilot projects; and
best practices regarding the use of public-private partnerships to improve the effectiveness of public benefit programs to address food insecurity and poverty.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations
children.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $5,000,000 to remain available until expended.

children.heading: Appropriation in advance
children.text: Only funds appropriated under paragraph (1) in advance specifically to carry out this section shall be available to carry out this section.
